Triage (finding concentration round): promoted to `pm:queue` · type Task. Fourth instance found by a fourth person is the tell that per-instance discovery has failed; the proposed shrink-only ledger mirrors the #10665 `KNOWN_IMPORT_UNSAFE` precedent exactly, costs nothing in fabricated pairs, and bounds the currently-unbounded `silent`-bucket population. Dispatch note: ⛔ the `:920` refusal itself stays (the +139084 measurement stands, per the card); building the ledger requires enumerating the silent-bucket instances, so expect M. Serial note: #10314 (bare `examples`, open, in-flight with the devx seat) remains a valid individual fix — the ledger entry for it should reflect whichever lands first. `mode:subagent`, opus; Clause-②: no.

## A fifth instance, and it is a different kind from the four

Recorded from today's #10619 work (PR #10774, a brand-new gate landing now), because it changes what this card is arguing rather than just adding a row.

The four instances in the body are **archaeology** — gates that were already unnameable, each discovered by someone reading the residue block on the way past. This one is **prospective**: a gate written today would have joined the population *on the day it landed*, and did not only because its author knew about the trap in advance.

Verified in the source rather than taken from the report — `scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs:157-163` on that PR's head:

```js
/**
 * It is spelled as a glob and not as the bare word `packages` on purpose:
 * `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` refuses a bare single-segment hint as too
 * generic, so a gate that declares its population that way is unnameable by any
 * dispatch derivation and lands already invisible.
 */
const POPULATION = 'packages/**';
```

*"Lands already invisible"* is a sharper statement of this card's point than the body currently makes, and it was written by someone hitting the constraint head-on, not reviewing it.

The author then verified nameability explicitly rather than assuming it:

```
$ node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs packages/plugins/plugin-reports/src/reports-plugin.ts
  - node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs   [lint.yml]   matched via
    packages/plugins/plugin-reports/src/reports-plugin.ts ⇢ gate source 'packages/**'
```

### What this changes

The body reads as *"4 gates need cleaning up, found one at a time."* The accurate framing is that **the class reproduces at the rate new gates are written.** Every gate whose natural population is a top-level directory — `packages`, `apps`, `examples`, `scripts`, `content` — is one bare word away from landing silent, and the only thing standing between a new gate and that outcome is whether its author happens to have read the residue block or a card like this one. Cleaning up the existing 4 does not close it.

### A point in the proposed remedy's favour

The shrink-only ledger direction **does** cover the prospective case, and that is worth stating explicitly since the body does not: if a separator-less population literal whose first segment the tree has must either declare its subtree spelling or appear on a ledger that **nothing new can join**, then a new gate spelling a bare word fails at authoring time instead of landing invisible. That is a stronger argument for the ledger than the four historical instances are — those could equally be fixed one at a time, and have been. This one cannot.

⛔ Unchanged: this is still not a request to touch the `:920` refusal. The +139084 measurement stands, and the escape working exactly as documented is what today's gate demonstrates.

Still `pm:queue`, unassigned, not dispatched — the direction is a taxonomy call, not something to self-dispatch.

## A working in-repo precedent for the escape, from a gate that landed today

Carried over from #10790 (closed as a duplicate of this card), because it is more concrete than anything either card currently names:

> the remedy is the `ROOT_DIR_WATCH_HINTS` subtree-declaration pattern `check-role-word.mjs` already uses for `skills/**`

This card's body describes the escape abstractly — *"a gate whose population really is a root file reaches it by declaring the subtree spelling"* — and cites #10114 as the first instance. The `ROOT_DIR_WATCH_HINTS` spelling is that escape as a **named, copyable idiom** rather than a one-off, in a gate whose own work was in flight today. Whoever takes the ledger direction should lift that shape rather than invent a third one.

### And a sixth instance, arriving the same way the other five did

`check:parse-guard` (instance #4 in this card's table) was hit again today by an agent working #10533 — a *different* card, a *different* seat — who ran the gate by hand precisely because the derivation would not name it, then filed it fresh as #10790 without knowing this card existed.

That is two independent agents hitting the same wall within one hour, on unrelated work. It is also the second time today this card's argument has been made for it by events rather than by argument: the fifth instance (recorded above) was a **new** gate that would have landed silent had its author not known, and this sixth is a **re-discovery** of an instance already enumerated here.

The two failure modes are now both demonstrated live:
- **discovery cost** — the class is re-found one instance at a time, because nothing enumerates it (this instance);
- **reproduction rate** — new gates keep joining it, because nothing refuses a bare literal at authoring time (the fifth).

A shrink-only ledger addresses both. Nothing else on the card's direction list addresses either.

⛔ Still unchanged: this is not a request to touch the `:920` refusal. The +139084 measurement stands.

## What this dispatch inherits, read rather than counted

I have read all three comments on this card. Carried forward verbatim:

- **The `:920` refusal STAYS.** The +139084-fabricated-pair measurement in `hintCovers`' own docblock stands. This card is a ledger, not a loosening. Any diff that touches that condition is out of scope.
- **The idiom already exists — lift it, do not invent a third.** `check-role-word.mjs`'s `ROOT_DIR_WATCH_HINTS = ['skills/**']` is the escape as a named, copyable shape (carried over from #10790, closed as a duplicate of this card). #10662 / #10687 took the same escape for `check:doc-authoring` and `check:doc-formula-expressions`.
- **The class reproduces prospectively, not just archaeologically.** `scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs:157-163` (landed today, PR #10774) spells `POPULATION = 'packages/**'` with a docblock saying a gate declaring the bare word *"lands already invisible"*. A ledger has to bound the future population, not only enumerate the four known rows.
- **Precedent to mirror:** `KNOWN_IMPORT_UNSAFE` (#10665) — shrink-only, enumerated, costs nothing in fabricated pairs.

## Serial constraints cleared at claim time

`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is held by **no open PR**. ⚠️ #10314 (bare `examples`, the individual fix for instance 1) may still be in flight: **the ledger row for `check:examples-live-imports` must reflect whichever lands first** — if #10314 has landed by the time you branch, that row is already discharged and the ledger must say so rather than re-listing it.

## Mandatory before you write code

Re-derive the population on today's `main` (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs <path>`) — the body's 4-row table was measured at `47cd3ec1f8` (09:09:54Z) and at least two gates have landed since. The `silent` bucket (79 of 125 families at measurement) is where the unbounded remainder lives; enumerate it rather than trusting the body's four.

## Standing constraints

- Governed, human-merge-only: `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` — propose wording in the report instead.
- Never edit `content/docs/releases/**`.
- #9465 fence: `.changeset/**` config and changeset scripts, `cut-rc.yml`, `release.yml`, `pr-automation.yml` changeset steps, root `package.json`. An individual `.changeset/<name>.md` entry file is NOT fenced.
- Never `git stash` — `refs/stash` is shared across every worktree.
- Never write `--` when passing args to vitest through pnpm: `pnpm --filter <pkg> test --maxWorkers=2 <file>`. pnpm forwards the separator verbatim and vitest's `cac` silently discards everything after it.
- A pipe swallows the exit code. Capture as `cmd > log 2>&1; ec=$?`.

Report back to me; I review against GitHub and land it.
